title: Order Axioms
summary: Order axioms specify betweenness on a line and how a line separates the rest of the plane.
statements: If B lies between A and C, then A, B, and C are distinct collinear points, and B also lies between C and A.
For distinct points A and C, there is a point B on line AC such that C lies between A and B.
Of any three distinct collinear points, exactly one lies between the other two.

Plane Separation Axiom: every line divides the points not on it into two nonempty, disjoint half-planes. A segment joining two points in the same half-plane does not meet the line; a segment joining points in opposite half-planes meets the line in exactly one point.

historicalContext.title: From diagrams to order axioms
paragraphs: Euclid often relied on the reader to see from a diagram how points lie between one another and how a line crosses a triangle. In 1882, Moritz Pasch argued that these order facts must be stated independently of the picture.

Hilbert's 1899 Foundations of Geometry incorporated explicit order axioms. This app uses plane separation as a strong modern formulation, making Pasch's triangle-crossing principle a theorem rather than an additional axiom.

whatItEnables: You can extend segments, reason without relying on the appearance of a diagram, and justify same-side, opposite-side, ray, and angle-interior arguments. Plane separation also implies Pasch's triangle-crossing property: a line that enters a triangle through one side and avoids the vertices must leave through another side.
